newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index fell 3.649 points or 4.55 percent to 80.685 on Wednesday due to profit-taking after the surges of recent weeks, traders said.
Volume was heavy at 95 million shares worth $44 million.
"After the rise in recent weeks, heavy profit-taking, especially of cheap stocks, set in today, depressing the market," one trader said.

"Today's loss was a technical correction partly sparked by a fall on the Shenzhen market," said a second trader. "The correction is likely to continue for the rest of this week. But market sentiment is good and the index will recover next week."
Shenzhen's B index lost 3.83 percent today on talk of tighter control over local investors trading B shares, traders said.

Shenzhen securities authorities have warned brokerages in the city not to allow local investors to buy B shares unless the money comes from outside the country, an official of the Shenzhen Securities Management Office said on Wednesday.
Brokers in Shanghai said they did not know of any such notice being distributed to brokers in Shanghai. Officials of the central bank and the national regulator in Beijing declined to comment.
All 42 Shanghai B shares traded, with 34 down, one flat and seven up.
"Investors began to be concerned about possible measures by Beijing to ban domestic investors from buying," one broker said.

"Technical charts indicate the market has entered a correction phase and the index is likely to test the 75-point support level," a second broker said. "The market trend mainly depends on the attitude of the securities authorities," he added.
Cheap stocks with poor results led the falls after speculative jumps in the past few days, brokers said.
Shanghai Erfangji was the biggest loser, plunging $0.060 or 21.42 percent to $0.220, on volume of 3.8 million shares.

Shanghai Rubber Belt followed, tumbling $0.054 or 17.08 percent to $0.262, on volume of 718,000 shares. Shanghai Jintai traded the most on institutional liquidation, down $0.012 or 4.28 percent to $0.268, on volume of 6.2 million shares.
Shanghai A share index rallied after falls on Tuesday but the market was still in a mood of consolidation amid uncertainty over its direction, brokers said.

The index rose 17.559 points or 1.37 percent to 1301.322 points, on volume of 1.1 billion shares worth 13.8 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index jumped 99.013 points or 3.34 percent to 3064.238 points.
